vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: agentcanary
Version: 1.0.0

The OpenClaw AgentSkills bundle for 'agentcanary' is classified as benign. Both SKILL.md and endpoints.md consistently describe an API-only skill that performs HTTP GET requests to retrieve market intelligence. The documentation explicitly states 'no local execution, no binaries, no shell commands, no filesystem access, no secrets in the prompt, read-only'. There is no evidence of prompt injection attempts, data exfiltration, malicious execution, persistence mechanisms, or obfuscation. The instructions provided are solely for how an AI agent should interact with the described external API for market analysis, aligning with its stated purpose.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent: it documents an API-only market-intelligence service, requests no installs or credentials, and its runtime instructions stay within that scope.

dimensions.detail: Name/description claim an API market-intelligence service and the SKILL.md/endpoints.md exclusively describe HTTP GET endpoints, read-only feeds, and cadence guidance — all coherent with the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are limited to calling documented endpoints, cadence guidance, and using the API as a risk gate. There are no instructions to read files, access environment variables, run shell commands, or send data to unexpected endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — instruction-only surface, so nothing is written to disk or installed. This is the lowest-risk install model.

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and low-risk as described, but before installing: 1) verify the operator and the agentcanary.ai domain (phishing/impersonation risk), 2) confirm the future billing/auth model so you don't need to paste secrets into prompts (wallet signatures are preferable), 3) start with minimal privileges and test read-only calls only, and 4) if you plan to let an autonomous agent act on these signals for trading, enforce a safety layer (e.g., require human confirmation or separate execution credentials) — market-intel can influence financial actions, so control the agent's execution scope.
